newsitem.title: USA: Death of Malcolm X widow ruled a homicide.
newsitem.headline: Death of Malcolm X widow ruled a homicide.

text.p: New York City's medical examiner ruled on Tuesday that the death of Malcolm X's widow Betty Shabazz, who succumbed on Monday to burns suffered in a fire, was a homicide.

The fire was allegedly set by her troubled 12-year-old grandson. Westchester County, New York, prosecutors said they would not reveal whether murder charges were filed against the boy, named Malcolm after his grandfather.
"It is a closed confidential Family Court matter, and it would be improper to disclose any details," said Jim Doughty, spokesman for the Westchester County Attorney.

Shabazz died on Monday from burns she suffered in a fire in her Yonkers, New York, apartment on June 1. The widow of the slain civil rights leader was burned on more than 80 percent of her body, and doctors had performed five skin-graft operations.
Police say her grandson, who was staying with his grandmother, set the blaze with gasoline. He was charged with juvenile delinquency after the fire.
Family attorney Percy Sutton said he expected additional charges would be filed against the boy.
He said if convicted the boy would face 18 months in detention due to his young age, although a judge could extend his sentence until he reached age 18.
The boy has been held in a juvenile detention centre since the fire.
Funeral arrangements remained incomplete, and the Shabazz family said it would announce plans on Wednesday.

Shabazz, an activist for black women and a champion for human rights, was sitting in the audience with their four young daughters when her husband was gunned down at Harlem's Audubon Ballroom on Feb. 21, 1965. She had twin girls after his death.
A trained nurse, she earned a doctorate in education, and served as public relations administrator at Medgar Evers College in Brooklyn, New York, at her death.
